tips: Test pollution: one test leaves state another depends on — shuffling reveals this.
Fixed seeds for randomness aren't 'fixed' across runtimes — verify on CI's runtime.
Snapshots can differ by line endings — `.gitattributes` to enforce LF.

guides.title: CI: build works locally, fails in CI
steps: Match runtime versions: pin Node/Python/etc. in CI config to what you use locally.
Clean install locally to compare: `rm -rf node_modules && npm ci`.
Use `npm ci` (not `install`) in CI to honor the lockfile exactly.
Check for case-sensitivity in imports — Linux is strict.
Check for env vars baked into local builds (`.env.local`) not present in CI.
Increase verbosity: pass `--verbose` or set CI=true to enable diagnostic flags many tools use.
tips: `npm ci` is reproducible; `npm install` may bump packages.
.env files generally shouldn't be in the repo; CI uses secrets.
Build caches in CI can mask issues — try a clean run to confirm.

triggers: works on mac fails on linux
guides.title: Cross-platform: works on Mac, fails on Linux
steps: Case sensitivity: macOS is usually case-insensitive; Linux is strict. Fix any case-mismatched imports/paths.
Line endings: macOS uses LF (good), Windows CRLF can sneak in via Git config — set `core.autocrlf` correctly.
GNU vs BSD coreutils: `sed`, `awk`, `xargs` flags differ. Use `gsed`/`gawk` locally or write POSIX-only.
File paths: hard-coded `/Users/...` won't exist on Linux. Use env vars or relative paths.
Permissions: Linux is stricter; ensure executables have +x and aren't on noexec mounts.
Test in Docker (linux container) before pushing — avoid all surprises.
tips: GNU sed in-place: `sed -i 's/x/y/' file`. BSD/Mac requires: `sed -i '' 's/x/y/' file`. Painful.
Filesystem case-insensitivity on Mac hides 'should-fail' imports — Linux exposes them.
A Linux dev container in VS Code reproduces CI locally with minimal setup.

guides.title: Encoding: UTF-8 / BOM issues
steps: Detect a BOM: `head -c 3 file | xxd` — `efbbbf` is the BOM.
Strip a BOM: `sed -i '1s/^\xEF\xBB\xBF//' file` (GNU sed) or rewrite the file in your editor without BOM.
Detect encoding: `file -i file.txt` shows it.
Convert encoding: `iconv -f WINDOWS-1252 -t UTF-8 in.txt > out.txt`.
If parsing JSON/YAML, a BOM causes 'unexpected character' errors at column 1.
Set editor to 'UTF-8 without BOM' for source files.
tips: Windows Notepad adds a BOM by default — switch tools.
YAML and JSON spec forbid BOMs — many parsers tolerate them, some don't.
VS Code: bottom bar shows encoding; click to re-save without BOM.

guides.title: General: time zone bug
steps: First rule: store all times as UTC. Convert only at display time.
Identify where the time is coming from: DB, API, system clock.
Check the server's TZ: `date` and `cat /etc/timezone`.
Set TZ explicitly in your runtime (TZ env var, container, etc.) — UTC for servers is standard.
When formatting for users, convert to their TZ at the boundary, not in the middle of logic.
If date appears 'one day off', it's often a UTC midnight crossing — check the time component too.
tips: Beware: JS `new Date('2024-01-01')` parses as UTC; `new Date('2024-01-01T00:00')` as LOCAL. Subtle.
Always test around DST transitions — bugs hide there.
Use libraries (luxon, date-fns-tz, pytz) instead of rolling your own TZ math.

guides.title: General: off-by-one error
steps: Print the boundaries: start, end, length, what's at index 0 and at index length-1.
Identify the language's slice semantics: most are half-open ([start, end)).
Sketch a small example by hand for n=0, n=1, n=2 — see when it breaks.
Common: confusing length with last index (length is N, last index is N-1).
Common: using `<=` where you meant `<` (or vice versa).
Common: iterating one beyond a sentinel that should stop you.
tips: Prefer iterators (`for x in xs`) over manual indices when possible.
Write a test for empty input, single element, and 'standard' cases — off-by-ones surface here.
Fence-post problem: N posts make N-1 fence sections.

guides.title: General: intermittent / flaky test
steps: Run it many times: `for i in 1..100; pytest -x test_foo.py`. Get a real failure rate.
Identify the category: time/async race, ordering dependence, shared resource, randomness.
Fix async races: await every promise; remove arbitrary sleeps in favor of proper waits.
Fix order dependence: isolate state, run tests in random order to expose.
Fix shared resources: unique ports, unique DB schemas per test, clean up always.
Pin random seeds at test boundaries.
tips: Quarantine, then fix — don't merge new code on a flaky baseline.
Retries hide flakiness; only use them as a temporary measure.
If a test passes alone but fails in suite, it's almost always shared state.

guides.title: General: env var not loading
steps: Confirm the file is named exactly `.env` (no extension, hidden) in the right directory.
Confirm your framework loads it: Next.js auto-loads from project root; Node needs `dotenv` imported FIRST.
Import order matters: `require('dotenv').config()` MUST be before any code that reads `process.env`.
For deployment, set env vars in the platform (Vercel, Heroku, Docker) — `.env` files often aren't deployed.
Print to verify: `console.log('X=', process.env.MY_VAR)` early in startup.
Reserved-prefix gotchas: CRA needs `REACT_APP_`; Vite needs `VITE_`; Next.js needs `NEXT_PUBLIC_` for client-side.
tips: Don't commit `.env` — add to .gitignore. Commit `.env.example` with empty values as documentation.
Trailing whitespace and quotes in env values cause silent bugs — strip both.
`direnv` auto-loads .env when you cd in — great for terminals.

guides.title: Build: Node version mismatch
steps: Read `engines` in package.json — it specifies required Node range.
Check your version: `node -v` and your CI's version.
Install the matching version: `nvm install <version> && nvm use <version>`.
Add a `.nvmrc` file with the version so collaborators auto-switch.
In CI, pin: `actions/setup-node@v4` with `node-version-file: '.nvmrc'`.
Reinstall deps after switching: `rm -rf node_modules && npm ci`.
tips: `engines` in package.json is documentation; npm doesn't enforce unless you set `engine-strict=true`.
Lockfile resolution can change with Node version — `npm ci` failures often trace here.
Volta is an alternative to nvm — auto-switches per project.

guides.title: Mobile: site broken on phone
steps: Confirm meta viewport is set: `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`.
Open Chrome DevTools → device toolbar (Cmd+Shift+M) to simulate phones.
Inspect overflow: 100vw containers + scrollbars cause horizontal scroll. Use `max-width: 100%`.
Check fixed pixel widths in CSS — switch to %, rem, or vw/vh.
Touch targets too small: minimum 44x44px per Apple HIG.
Test on a real device — emulators miss touch and font-rendering issues.
tips: Safari iOS has its own quirks — test there too, not just Chrome's emulator.
100vh on iOS Safari includes the URL bar — use `dvh` (dynamic) or JS fallback.
BrowserStack/Sauce Labs let you test real devices remotely.

guides.title: Deploy: SPA routes 404 on refresh
steps: Recognize: the URL works when you navigate from the home page, but refresh on a deep link 404s.
Reason: the server tries to serve `/some/route` as a file, doesn't find it, returns 404.
Configure the server to serve `index.html` for ALL routes (SPA fallback).
Apache: `.htaccess` with `FallbackResource /index.html`.
Nginx: `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;`.
Static hosts (Netlify, Vercel) usually have a SPA toggle or `_redirects` / `vercel.json` config.
tips: Netlify: add `_redirects` with `/* /index.html 200`.
Vercel/Next.js: routing is handled, but for static export ensure rewrites.
Hash-based routing (`#/path`) sidesteps this entirely but isn't SEO-friendly.

guides.title: General: missing logs in production
steps: Check the log level: `LOG_LEVEL=info` or similar. Many frameworks default to warn/error in prod.
Make sure your log calls match: `logger.info(...)` won't appear if level is `warn`.
Confirm logs are flushed: synchronous on startup/shutdown, async during runtime.
Check where logs go: stdout, file, log service. Some platforms only capture stdout.
If using JSON logging, ensure your viewer can parse the structure.
For ephemeral containers, ship logs to a central service — they're gone on restart.
tips: 12-factor: log to stdout, let the platform handle aggregation.
Buffered logging can drop the last messages on crash — use sync logging at shutdown.
Sentry/Datadog/CloudWatch all work — pick one before you're firefighting.

guides.title: General: CRLF line endings break shell scripts
steps: Recognize the symptom: 'bad interpreter: No such file or directory' or `^M` in error output.
Confirm with `file script.sh` — 'with CRLF line terminators' is the giveaway.
Convert: `dos2unix script.sh` (if installed), or `sed -i 's/\r$//' script.sh`.
Configure git to use LF in repo: in `.gitattributes` add `*.sh text eol=lf`.
Set Git globally: `git config --global core.autocrlf input` on Linux/Mac; `true` on Windows.
Renormalize: `git add --renormalize . && git commit -m 'normalize line endings'`.
tips: Editors on Windows default to CRLF; force LF via editor settings or .editorconfig.
.editorconfig: `end_of_line = lf` is the durable answer.
WSL plus mounted Windows drives is a common source of mixed endings.

guides.title: General: it worked yesterday, broken today
steps: What changed? List every variable: code, deps, OS update, certificate expiry, time of day, DST switch.
If code changed, `git log --since=yesterday` shows commits. `git bisect` if many.
If deps changed: `npm ls --depth=0` or `pip freeze` — diff against yesterday's snapshot.
If env changed: a system update, an OS upgrade, a TLS cert expiry, a token rotation.
If time-based: DST switches, midnight UTC crossings, monthly cert renewals.
If nothing 'changed', check disk, memory, free file handles — silent resource exhaustion.
tips: git bisect is gold for code regressions — it finds the exact bad commit in log(N) steps.
TLS cert expiry is the #1 cause of 'nothing changed and it broke'.
Snapshot deps with a lockfile so 'what changed' is answerable.

guides.title: Git: clone slow or fails
steps: Try a shallow clone: `git clone --depth 1 <url>` — only latest commit.
If specific branch: `git clone --depth 1 --branch <name> <url>`.
If hanging on resolving deltas, raise buffer: `git config --global http.postBuffer 524288000`.
If a huge repo, try partial clone: `git clone --filter=blob:none <url>`.
Check network — try fetching one file from the repo via curl.
If SSH, try HTTPS as an alternative (or vice versa).
tips: Shallow clones can't push easily — unshallow with `git fetch --unshallow` if needed.
Some networks throttle long-lived TCP — pause/resume by checking out shallowly first.
Mirrors (e.g. GitHub Enterprise + LFS proxy) sometimes are faster than the canonical host.

guides.title: Python: making sense of a long traceback
steps: Read from the BOTTOM — the most useful line is the last exception type and message.
Walk up frame-by-frame: each entry is a stack level, the topmost is where Python started.
Look for the first frame in YOUR code (skip library internals).
If you see 'During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred', the lower one is the trigger; the upper is the cascade.
Use `traceback.print_exc()` in catch blocks to capture the full chain.
For exceptions in threads, install a `threading.excepthook` to surface them.
tips: rich (`pip install rich`) pretty-prints tracebacks with locals — game-changer for debugging.
Chained exceptions use `from`: `raise NewError(...) from original_err` preserves context cleanly.
`sys.exception()` in 3.11+ gets the current exception without explicit args.

guides.title: General: no space left on device
steps: Check disk usage: `df -h` — find the full filesystem.
If filesystem isn't full but you still get the error, check inodes: `df -i`.
Find big stuff: `du -sh /* 2>/dev/null | sort -h` (top-level), drill down into the biggest.
Common culprits: logs (`/var/log`), Docker (`/var/lib/docker`), build caches, node_modules everywhere.
Clean Docker: `docker system prune -a`.
Clean homebrew caches, npm caches, pip caches as appropriate.
tips: `ncdu` is an interactive du — much faster to navigate.
Lots of tiny files = inode exhaustion even with disk space free.
Truncate, don't delete, active log files: `truncate -s 0 file.log` keeps the file handle alive.

guides.title: General: too many open files
steps: Check current limit: `ulimit -n`.
Raise it for this shell: `ulimit -n 65535`.
Persist: in `/etc/security/limits.conf` add `* soft nofile 65535` (and hard).
On macOS, add `kern.maxfiles` and `kern.maxfilesperproc` to `/etc/sysctl.conf` or a launchd plist.
Find the leak in your app: not closing sockets/files in a loop. Use `lsof -p <pid>` to see what's open.
Most languages have explicit close calls or context managers — use them rigorously.
tips: 1024 is the default on many systems — way too low for any real server.
Connection pools that don't release connections are a classic leak.
Each TCP connection = one file descriptor.

guides.title: Python/pytest: print statements not showing
steps: By default pytest captures stdout. Disable with `pytest -s`.
Or run with `--capture=no` for the same effect explicitly.
On failure, captured output is shown by default — only on PASS is it hidden.
If you really need real-time output, `-s --log-cli-level=DEBUG`.
Use `caplog` fixture to inspect captured logs in assertions.
Use `capsys` fixture to inspect captured stdout/stderr in assertions.
tips: `-s` is the most-used pytest flag for interactive debugging.
If you need a debugger, `pytest --pdb` drops into pdb on failure.
`pytest -x` stops at the first failure — great for iterating.

guides.title: JS: works in dev, fails in prod (devDependency)
steps: Check the failing import — is the package in `dependencies` or `devDependencies`?
Production installs (`npm ci --production`, `NODE_ENV=production npm install`) skip devDependencies.
If the package is needed at runtime, move it to `dependencies`: `npm install <pkg> --save`.
If it's only build-time, ensure your build step runs before pruning devDeps.
For Docker: keep devDeps during build stage, prune in final stage.
Verify with `npm ls <pkg>` — should show it as not-dev-only.
tips: Common mistake: TypeScript/babel in devDeps, runtime helpers also there. Move runtime helpers out.
`npm prune --production` removes devDeps from an existing install — useful after build.
Multi-stage Docker: build in one stage with all deps, copy to slim runtime stage.

guides.title: General: pipe terminal output to clipboard
steps: macOS: `echo hello | pbcopy` — clipboard now has 'hello'. Paste with `pbpaste`.
Linux X11: install xclip, then `echo hello | xclip -selection clipboard`.
Linux Wayland: `wl-copy` and `wl-paste`.
Windows (Git Bash): `echo hello | clip.exe`.
WSL: `echo hello | clip.exe` reaches the Windows clipboard.
Make it a function: `alias clip='pbcopy'` (or distro equivalent) for muscle memory.
tips: Tmux 'copy mode' captures terminal output into its own buffer — sync to system clipboard with config.
iTerm2 (Mac) can auto-copy on selection — saves keystrokes.
`pbpaste | command` is great for processing whatever you copied.

guides.title: Python: sys.path / PYTHONPATH issues
steps: Print sys.path: `python -c 'import sys; print(sys.path)'`. Note your cwd is usually `''` in the list.
If your local module isn't on sys.path, run from the project root, or add `PYTHONPATH=src python ...`.
Better: install your package in editable mode: `pip install -e .` with a `pyproject.toml`.
Or use `python -m mymodule` instead of `python path/to/mymodule.py` — the `-m` adds the package's root to sys.path correctly.
Add `__init__.py` to make a folder a real package (or PEP 420 namespace if you skip it).
Avoid mucking with `sys.path` from your code — fix the install instead.
tips: `pip install -e .` is the right way to make local imports work — no path hacks needed.
`python -m` is much more reliable than running scripts directly for path resolution.
Layout matters: src layout vs flat layout has different gotchas.

guides.title: JS/React: too many re-renders
steps: Read the error: 'Maximum update depth exceeded' or 'Too many re-renders'.
Look for state updates IN render: calling `setX()` directly in the function body re-runs render forever.
Move state updates into event handlers or useEffect.
Check useEffect deps: an object/array in deps recreated each render triggers infinite effects. Memoize with useMemo or extract primitives.
Check that event handlers aren't called by mistake (e.g. `onClick={handler()}` calls; `onClick={handler}` references).
Add `console.log('render')` at the top of the component to count renders.
Use React DevTools Profiler to see what's re-rendering.
tips: Most infinite-render bugs are 'I called setX during render' — search for setX outside callbacks.
An object literal in deps `[{ foo: 1 }]` is a new reference every render — useMemo it.
useCallback for handlers passed to memoized children.

guides.title: Python: PicklingError
steps: Read the error — it names what can't be pickled (often a lambda, local function, or thread lock).
Replace lambdas with top-level functions.
Don't pass module-level resources (open files, connections) across processes — open them in the worker.
For `multiprocessing`, switch to `dill` (`import dill as pickle`) which handles more cases — or use `multiprocess` library.
For `concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor`, the same restriction applies.
Consider switching to threads if the work is I/O bound and pickling is the blocker.
tips: Pickling rules: top-level callables only, no open OS handles, no thread locks.
`__reduce__` lets you define how a class pickles if needed.
Cloudpickle (used by Dask, Ray) is broader than stdlib pickle — sometimes a drop-in fix.

guides.title: Python/Jupyter: kernel keeps dying
steps: Open the terminal that launched Jupyter — kernel crashes log there.
If OOM, free memory or downsize data. Check with `htop`.
If a native lib segfaults, isolate which import — comment out and run a minimal cell.
Numpy/scipy/torch built against different BLAS can crash on import — match versions.
On Apple Silicon, mixed arm64/x86 wheels can crash — reinstall everything for one architecture.
Update ipykernel: `pip install --upgrade ipykernel`.
tips: Kernel logs are in `~/.jupyter` or printed to the launching terminal — check both.
If it crashes on import, that import is incompatible with another in the env.
Fresh venv + reinstall is faster than tracking down a binary mismatch.

guides.title: Git: track a remote branch
steps: On a new local branch, first push: `git push -u origin <branch>` sets upstream and pushes.
For an existing branch: `git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/<branch>`.
Confirm: `git branch -vv` shows tracking info per branch.
After upstream is set, `git push` and `git pull` work without args.
To switch what a branch tracks: `git branch --set-upstream-to=<new-remote>/<new-branch>`.
tips: `push.autoSetupRemote=true` in config means `git push` of a new branch sets upstream automatically.
`git fetch` updates remote-tracking refs (origin/main) without touching your local branches.
`git remote -v` shows the URL behind each remote name.

guides.title: Network: intermittent / flaky connectivity
steps: Run `mtr <host>` for a few minutes — it pings AND traceroutes continuously, showing packet loss per hop.
If loss appears at a specific hop, that hop is the problem.
Test at different times — ISP congestion has patterns.
Test from a different network (phone hotspot) to isolate your network vs the destination.
Check DNS resolver — sometimes DNS times out while reachability is fine: `dig +stats <host>`.
If wireless, test wired to isolate Wi-Fi as cause.
tips: `mtr` is the single best tool for intermittent issues — better than ping or traceroute alone.
Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 or Google's 8.8.8.8 as a test DNS isolates resolver issues.
Wi-Fi interference (2.4 GHz especially) is wildly underestimated as a cause.

guides.title: Python: new-feature syntax errors on old Python
steps: Confirm Python version: `python --version`.
Map: walrus `:=` needs 3.8+; positional-only `/` needs 3.8+; `match` needs 3.10+; PEP 695 generics need 3.12+; type statements need 3.12+.
f-strings need 3.6+; nested f-strings with quotes need 3.12+.
If supporting old versions, rewrite without the feature OR raise the minimum.
Set `python_requires` in setup.cfg/pyproject.toml to enforce.
Use `pyupgrade` to add new syntax automatically once you bump the minimum.
tips: End-of-life Pythons (3.7 and older) are commonly broken — drop support unless required.
ruff/mypy can be configured to your minimum version and warn on incompatible usage.
vermin scans a codebase for the minimum Python version actually required by the syntax used.

guides.title: JS: silent promise / async failure
steps: Find the async call — look for a missing `await` or `.catch`.
Wrap awaits in try/catch: `try { await x() } catch (e) { ... }`.
Chain `.catch()` on every promise where you don't have try/catch.
In Node, install a global handler: `process.on('unhandledRejection', e => console.error(e))`.
In the browser: `window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', e => ...)`.
Forgot to return a promise from an arrow body? `() => asyncFn()` returns the promise; `() => { asyncFn() }` swallows it.
tips: Implicit-return arrows propagate the inner promise; block-body arrows need explicit `return`.
ESLint's `no-floating-promises` (TypeScript-ESLint) catches every dangling promise.
Top-level await in ESM removes a lot of swallow-prone patterns.

guides.title: Network: debugging an HTTP request with curl
steps: Start with `-v`: `curl -v https://api.example.com/path` — shows TLS, headers, response.
Show only response headers: `curl -I <url>`.
Save body to a file: `curl -o body.json <url>` so the terminal isn't flooded.
Send custom headers: `-H 'Authorization: Bearer X' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'`.
POST JSON: `-X POST -d '{"k":"v"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'`.
Follow redirects: `-L`. Trace timings: `-w '%{time_total}\n' -o /dev/null -s`.
tips: `httpie` is a friendlier alternative for ad-hoc testing.
`curl --trace-ascii /dev/stdout` shows every byte sent and received — nuclear option.
`-w` format strings give you precise timing breakdowns (DNS, TLS, TTFB, total).
